evidence: app/server.mjs:1-4 — entire framework surface is serve, serveStatic, Hono, hono/html#html
app/server.mjs:37-40 — serveStatic with only root/path options, for 3 static files
app/package.json:11-13 — pins hono 4.13.14 (latest stable v4), @hono/node-server 2.1.5 (latest stable), htmx.org 2.0.11 (latest stable)
app/views/layout.mjs:2 — hono/html html tagged template, stable since Hono 3.x
reach.rationale: Only long-stable APIs are used, and the app correctly avoids the Hono v5 release candidate. The only nod toward the new is that the Node adapter is on v2, a major released ~6 months ago (2026-04-21) — but its public API is unchanged from v1, so this barely registers as reach.

evidence: app/server.mjs:37-40 — all framework-adapter usage sits in 4 lines at the top of one file
app/views/layout.mjs:1-40 — rendering helpers confined to one view module
app/lib/api.mjs:1-2 — own thin fetch/cache client instead of any framework-specific data layer
containment.rationale: There is nothing experimental to contain, and even the ordinary framework surface is centralized in server.mjs plus one view module; swapping the adapter or renderer would touch two files.

evidence: app/server.mjs:496 — htmx needed for the spec's type-as-you-search behavior (hx-trigger 'input changed delay:200ms')
app/server.mjs:238, 310 — htmx partial swaps for table sorting and game selection, replacing custom client JS
app/scripts/build.mjs:6-10 — vendor htmx at build time instead of a CDN dependency, the low-risk option
justification.rationale: No experimental API is used at all; every dependency choice buys something concrete (htmx for the required live-updating lists/tables, hono/html for auto-escaped templates) that a stable alternative would not.

findings.issue: The app rides @hono/node-server v2, a major released 2026-04-21 with a fast patch cadence (2.1.2/2.1.3/2.1.5 include a serveStatic path-decoding security fix, GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f).
findings.suggestion: Keep the exact pin (good for reproducibility) but watch node-server releases; the API surface used (serve, serveStatic) is unchanged from v1, so upgrades are low-effort.

findings.issue: app.onError uses the v4 signature (error, c); Hono v5 (currently 5.0.0-rc.1) changes it to (c, next) with c.error.
findings.suggestion: No action needed on hono 4.x; just note this in a migration checklist if the team ever moves to v5.

summary: This app uses zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs — its entire surface is long-stable Hono core, hono/html, the node-server adapter's serve/serveStatic, and core htmx attributes, all pinned to the latest stable releases (hono 4.13.14, @hono/node-server 2.1.5, htmx.org 2.0.11). It deliberately avoided the Hono v5 RC even though one exists. The only recency is the ~6-month-old node-server v2 major, whose public API is identical to v1, so swap risk is negligible.
